title: Relative Mayer–Vietoris gluing for the single-complex base-change map
statement: Let X' \xrightarrow{g'} X and S' \xrightarrow{g} S be a cartesian square with f:X\to S quasi-compact and quasi-separated and f':X'\to S' its base change [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-base-change]. Assume moreover that S and S' are affine. Let K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X) and K'\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{X'}) and let L(g')^*K\to K' be a map in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{X'}) [def-pc-derived-category]. Suppose X=U\cup V, where U and V are quasi-compact open subschemes and U\cap V is quasi-compact. For each W\in\{U,V,U\cap V\}, let W'=X'\times_X W and assume that the canonical composite Lg^*Rf_{W,*}(K|_W)\to Rf'_{W',*}L(g'|_{W'})^*(K|_W)\to Rf'_{W',*}(K'|_{W'}) is an isomorphism, using derived pullback and direct image [def-pc-derived-pullback, def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Then the canonical composite Lg^*Rf_*K\to Rf'_*L(g')^*K\to Rf'_*K' is an isomorphism. The canonical base-change maps are those of [def-pc-derived-base-change-map]; the map on each open is the restriction of the given map, transported by the canonical derived pullback composition isomorphisms [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition].

source.place: Tag 0DJ9, induction step; relative Mayer--Vietoris triangle from Cohomology, Lemma cohomology-lemma-unbounded-relative-mayer-vietoris

proof.text: Since S is affine and f is quasi-separated, X is quasi-separated, and X=U\cup V is quasi-compact (Tag 01KU, elementary). Since S and S' are affine, g is affine, hence so is its base change g' (Tag 01S5); thus U'=(g')^{-1}(U), V'=(g')^{-1}(V) are quasi-compact opens with X'=U'\cup V', and X' is quasi-compact and quasi-separated over the affine S'. So the derived Mayer--Vietoris triangle node applies to the cover X=U\cup V with E=K and to X'=U'\cup V' with E=K' [lem-pc-derived-mayer-vietoris-triangle]. Apply the exact functors Lg^*Rf_* and Rf'_* to these triangles and identify Rf_*R(j_W)_*=R(f|_W)_* and Rf'_*R(j_{W'})_*=R(f'|_{W'})_* for W\in\{U,V,U\cap V\} [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-composition]. This gives distinguished triangles in D(\mathcal O_{S'}) whose terms are Lg^*R(f|_W)_*(K|_W) and R(f'|_{W'})_*(K'|_{W'}) for W=X,U,V,U\cap V.

By the naturality node, applied with the same affine S and S' and the same cover [lem-pc-rf-mv-triangle-naturality], the comparison maps alpha_X, alpha_U direct-sum alpha_V, and alpha_{U intersect V} form a morphism from the first triangle of Step 1 to the second.

source.place: Tag 0DJ9, induction step; relative Mayer--Vietoris naturality

proof.text: By hypothesis, alpha_U and alpha_V are isomorphisms, so alpha_U direct-sum alpha_V is an isomorphism. The hypothesis for U intersect V says that alpha_{U intersect V} is an isomorphism. Applying the Mathlib two-out-of-three theorem for a morphism of distinguished triangles to these latter two components shows that alpha_X is an isomorphism.
For W=X, alpha_X is exactly the canonical composite Lg^*Rf_*K \to Rf'_*L(g')^*K \to Rf'_*K' appearing in the statement, so the preceding isomorphism is the required conclusion.
